newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SHARES END AT NEW RECORD AHEAD OF HOLIDAY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SHARES END AT NEW RECORD AHEAD OF HOLIDAY.

text.p: * The HEX index closes for Independence Day holiday up 0.49
percent at new 2471.14 life-high as market remains bullish. Some
risk of correction down seen but downside small, brokers say.
* Volume 430 million markka, 40 pct in Nokia.
* Advancers-decliners 45-30, 29 unchanged.
Shares set their fourth
consecutive record on Thursday and closed at the new peak for
Independence Day public and market holiday as the market
remained bullish, brokers said.
They saw some risk of a downward correction but low bond
yields continued to lend support altghough the long end of the
curve rose nine basis points in disappointment that German
Bundesbank did not trim its repo rate.
"I think there is a risk of a downward correction, but
shares keep rising as money burns holes in investors' pockets,"
one broker said.
Nokia closed 2.20 markka higher at 266.00 as the dollar
remained relatively strong and the greenback's level also helped
forestries hold gains posted earlier in the week.
The forestry index was up 0.12 percent with UPM-Kymmene flat
and Metsa-Serla B up 0.50 at 33.00 markka. Enso was also flat.
Orion rose to 163.00 markka -- its highest since June 19 and
closed up 3.50 markka at 161.00 as rumours that Investors had
sold its stake in Swedish Astra brought attention to Nordic
pharmaceuticals companies.
Finvest added 0.30 to 5.60 in lively trade on positive
recommendations from analysts.
Brokers said there were hopes that Nokia's improvement in
financial and logistic performance would help electronics
components makers like Finvest and Aspo, which rose 8.10 markka
or over four percent to a new 193.00 record.
The bourse said in a report that Finnish shares have
outperformed other Nordic bourses except Iceland clearly this
year -- up 41 percent since end-1995 compared to 33 percent for
Stockholm which was third. Still the downside was seen capped.
"The downside in Helsinki is limited as domestic interest
rates are low and fears of higher interest rates in the U.S.
have subsided," said one broker.
